$comment: Single source of truth for Intent Check install steps. Keyed tool > interface > os. Placeholders: {marketplace} = owner/repo; {ref} = '#name' when installing a branch/tag, empty otherwise. Copied by the prover site (scripts/sync-install-json.mjs).

prereqs: Claude Code installed
Node.js 18+ on PATH (check with `node -v`; install from nodejs.org or `brew install node`)
steps: Open Terminal in your project and run `claude`.
Run `/plugin marketplace add {marketplace}{ref}`.
Run `/plugin install intent@intentcomputing` and confirm the source when asked.
Run `/reload-plugins` (or restart Claude Code).
Send your first prompt: it shows a link to connect your account. Open it and approve.
macos.verify: Run `/intent:status`: it shows whether this machine is connected. Or ask Claude to change a function by 3+ lines and look for an `Intent Check:` note after the turn.
macos.update: Run `/plugin`, open Marketplaces, choose intentcomputing, and turn on auto-update (it is off by default for third-party marketplaces). To update once now, run `/plugin marketplace update intentcomputing`, then `/reload-plugins`.

prereqs: Codex CLI 0.147 or newer
Node.js 18+ on PATH (check with `node -v`; install from nodejs.org or `brew install node`)
steps: Open Terminal and run `codex plugin marketplace add {marketplace}{ref}`.
Run `codex plugin add intent@intentcomputing`.
Start `codex` and choose "Trust all and continue" when it says the plugin's hooks need review (or trust them in `/hooks`).
Send your first prompt: it shows a link to connect your account. Open it and approve.
macos.verify: Start `codex`, send a prompt, then ask the agent to run Intent Check status (it runs the plugin's `intent.js status`). Or ask it to change a function by 3+ lines: the check note arrives with your next message.
macos.update: Run `codex plugin marketplace upgrade intentcomputing`, then restart `codex`. Codex may ask you to trust the plugin's hooks again after an update. No auto-update setting is documented for Codex.
